Study.Metadata.Study.Name: Longitudinal Recovery Processes: 30-Day EMA Study
Study.Metadata.funding: National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) Grant R01DA000000
Study.Metadata.abstract: This study investigates the dynamic processes of substance use recovery through 30 days of ecological momentary assessment (EMA). Participants complete a baseline demographic assessment followed by twice-daily surveys (morning and evening) assessing positive affect, negative affect, substance cravings, and perceived social support. The design aims to capture within-person fluctuations and between-person differences in recovery trajectories over a one-month period.

AI.Information.AI.Generation.Prompt: Generate me a study looking to understand the longitudinal process of people in recovery using 30 days of EMA and a morning and evening survey. Include also a baseline assessment asking basic demographic questions. For the EMA assessments, ask about social support, cravings and negative and positive affect.

itemMap.Item.Text: How interested have you felt since waking up this morning?
itemMap.Conceptualization: Positive affect, specifically interest and engagement
itemMap.Modeling.Characteristics: Typically used as predictor or outcome in within-person analyses; may be averaged across days for between-person trait-level positive affect
itemMap.Scale.Name: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)
itemMap.Scoring: Single item 0-100 scale, or aggregated with other positive affect items for composite score
itemMap.Article.Title: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule
itemMap.Citation: Watson, D., Clark, L. A., & Tellegen, A. (1988). Development and validation of brief measures of positive and negative affect: The PANAS scales. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 54(6), 1063–1070. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.54.6.1063
itemMap.notes: Adapted from PANAS 'Interested' item for morning EMA delivery using VAS slider instead of Likert scale
